cli_cases.sql: CREATE TRIGGER tr BEFORE INSERT ON t FOR EACH ROW DELETE FROM audit_log

statement_sql: CREATE TRIGGER tr BEFORE INSERT ON t FOR EACH ROW DELETE FROM audit_log

cli_cases.notes: Golden path: one top-level trigger; the shared body audit emits the where blocker on member 0 with trigger scope metadata while the lifecycle notice stays at the trigger head.

cli_cases.sql: CREATE TRIGGER tr BEFORE INSERT ON t FOR EACH ROW UPDATE audit_log SET n = n + 1 WHERE id = NEW.id
cli_cases.notes: Safe body: WHERE-qualified UPDATE with a legal NEW.id reference audits cleanly; only the lifecycle notice fires.

cli_cases.sql: CREATE TRIGGER tr AFTER UPDATE ON t FOR EACH ROW BEGIN DELETE FROM audit_log; UPDATE t SET x = OLD.y WHERE id = 1; END
cli_cases.notes: Compound body: the first member DELETE lacks WHERE (blocker); the second member UPDATE carries WHERE and a legal OLD.y reference (no finding).

cli_cases.sql: CREATE TRIGGER tr BEFORE INSERT ON t FOR EACH ROW SET NEW.a = 1
cli_cases.notes: Legal pseudo-column: NEW.a on INSERT is event-legal and bound to the trigger target, not a missing table; the SET member is modelled so coverage stays complete.

cli_cases.sql: CREATE TRIGGER tr BEFORE INSERT ON t FOR EACH ROW UPDATE t SET x = OLD.y

unsupported_entries.reason: parsed by the shared parser but not covered by audited semantics

cli_cases.notes: Illegal pseudo-column: OLD on INSERT has no row image; the statement stays bounded incomplete rather than auditing a fabricated body. The illegal member stays bounded while the lifecycle notice still fires — siblings are never swallowed.

cli_cases.sql: CREATE TRIGGER tr AFTER DELETE ON t FOR EACH ROW INSERT INTO audit_log VALUES (NEW.id)

unsupported_entries.reason: parsed by the shared parser but not covered by audited semantics

cli_cases.notes: Illegal pseudo-column: NEW on DELETE has no new image; bounded incomplete for the same reason as OLD on INSERT. The illegal member stays bounded while the lifecycle notice still fires.

cli_cases.sql: CREATE TRIGGER tr BEFORE INSERT ON t FOR EACH ROW BEGIN DELETE FROM audit_log; UPDATE t SET x = OLD.y; END

unsupported_entries.reason: parsed by the shared parser but not covered by audited semantics

cli_cases.notes: Static risk and illegal pseudo-context stay separate: member 0 DELETE still blocks while member 1 OLD-under-INSERT stays bounded — the boundary never swallows sibling findings.

cli_cases.sql: CREATE DEFINER=`root`@`%` TRIGGER tr BEFORE DELETE ON t FOR EACH ROW DELETE FROM audit_log
cli_cases.notes: DEFINER clause is claimed as part of the trigger head; the body still audits through shared member analysis.

cli_cases.sql: CREATE TRIGGER tr BEFORE INSERT ON t FOR EACH ROW FOLLOWS other DELETE FROM audit_log
cli_cases.notes: Ordering attribute FOLLOWS (MySQL 8.0+) is modelled in the declaration; the body keeps auditing normally. Without a pinned target version the ordering clause is an explicit missing_target_version evidence gap rather than a silent pass.

cli_cases.sql: CREATE TRIGGER tr AFTER DELETE ON t FOR EACH ROW PRECEDES other DELETE FROM audit_log
cli_cases.notes: Ordering attribute PRECEDES is modelled symmetrically to FOLLOWS. Without a pinned target version the ordering clause is an explicit missing_target_version evidence gap rather than a silent pass.

cli_cases.sql: CREATE TRIGGER tr BEFORE INSERT ON t FOR EACH ROW FOLLOWS other DELETE FROM audit_log
cli_cases.notes: Version boundary: FOLLOWS/PRECEDES is a MySQL 5.7.2+ feature (WL#3253) — a 5.7.0 target is a determined negative blocker, distinct from a missing-version evidence gap.
DROP TRIGGER lifecycle is claimed and noticed; IF EXISTS is modelled.
